Magandang araw! I'm just flipping the dried fish on the bamboo mat so the afternoon sun dries them evenly. In our barangay, no one goes hungry as long as we share what we have.
I was just about to borrow a cup of coarse salt from Aling Rosa for tonight's tinola. Neighbors here always keep their doors open to each other.
When the church bells ring for six o'clock angelus, everyone stops whatever they're doing—even the children playing patintero—to offer a quiet prayer.
There used to be a quiet fisherman who'd drop off fresh galunggong at our porch whenever my husband was sick. He never asked for anything in return.
My Lola used to tell us: 'Don't whistle near the sea at night.' But honestly, as long as you treat people with kindness, the waters remain peaceful.
